arxiv-2112-02609.title: Computing Minimal Injective Resolutions of Sheaves on Finite Posets
arxiv-2112-02609.creator: Adam Brown and Ondřej Draganov
arxiv-2112-02609.description: Abstract In this paper we introduce two new methods for constructing injective resolutions of sheaves of finite-dimensional vector spaces on finite posets. Our main result is the existence and uniqueness of a minimal injective resolution of a given sheaf and an algorithm for its construction.

arxiv-2302-10023.creator: Linh Kästner, Reyk Carstens, Huajian Zeng, Jacek Kmiecik, Teham Bhuiyan, Niloufar Khorsandhi, Volodymyir Shcherbyna, Jens Lambrecht
arxiv-2302-10023.description: Abstract Following up on our previous works, in this paper, we present Arena-Rosnav 2.0 an extension to our previous works Arena-Bench [ 1 ] and Arena-Rosnav [ 2 ] , which adds a variety of additional modules for developing and benchmarking robotic navigation approaches.

arxiv-2403-12535.title: High-Fidelity SLAM Using Gaussian Splatting with Rendering-Guided Densification and Regularized Optimization
arxiv-2403-12535.creator: Shuo Sun, Malcolm Mielle, Achim J. Lilienthal, Martin Magnusson
arxiv-2403-12535.description: Abstract We propose a dense RGBD SLAM system based on 3D Gaussian Splatting that provides metrically accurate pose tracking and visually realistic reconstruction. To this end, we first propose a Gaussian densification strategy based on the rendering loss to map unobserved areas and refine reobserved areas.

arxiv-2406-11409.title: CodeGemma: Open Code Models Based on Gemma
arxiv-2406-11409.creator: CodeGemma Team, Google LLC
arxiv-2406-11409.description: Abstract This paper introduces CodeGemma, a collection of specialized open code models built on top of Gemma, capable of a variety of code and natural language generation tasks. We release three model variants. CodeGemma 7B pretrained (PT) and instruction-tuned (IT) variants have remarkably resilient natural language understanding, excel in mathematical reasoning, and match code capabilities of other open models.

arxiv-2506-13051.title: Stress-Testing Multimodal Foundation Models for Crystallographic Reasoning
arxiv-2506-13051.creator: Can Polat, Hasan Kurban, Erchin Serpedin, Mustafa Kurban, [1mm] Dept. of Electrical, Computer Engineering, Texas A&M University, College Station, TX, USA
arxiv-2506-13051.description: Abstract Evaluating foundation models for crystallographic reasoning requires benchmarks that isolate generalization behavior while enforcing physical constraints. This work introduces a multiscale multicrystal dataset with two physically grounded evaluation protocols to stress-test multimodal generative models. The Spatial-Exclusion benchmark withholds all supercells of a given radius from a diverse dataset, enabling controlled assessments of spatial interpolation and extrapolation.

arxiv-2602-02748.title: A Parametrized Complexity View on Robust Scheduling with Budgeted Uncertainty
arxiv-2602-02748.creator: Noam Goldberg, Dvir Shabtay
arxiv-2602-02748.description: Abstract In this study, we investigate a robust single-machine scheduling problem under processing time uncertainty. The uncertainty is modeled using the budgeted approach, where each job has a nominal and deviation processing time, and the number of deviations is bounded by Γ \Gamma . The objective is to minimize the maximum number of tardy jobs over all possible scenarios.

pmc-11536914.title: Evaluation of emergency nurses’ knowledge of medical response in nuclear and radiological emergencies : a cross-sectional study
pmc-11536914.creator: Nasser Shubayr
pmc-11536914.description: BackgroundEvaluating emergency room nurses’ knowledge of radiation protection, health effects, and decontamination procedures is crucial for preparedness in nuclear and radiological emergencies. pmc-12513097.title: Continuing medical education: understanding general practitioners who rarely attend, a cross-sectional questionnaire study among Danish GPs
pmc-12513097.creator: Helle Ibsen, Niels Kristian Kjaer, Jens Søndergaard, Igor Švab, Linda Juel Ahrenfeldt
pmc-12513097.description: BackgroundContinuing medical education (CME) is vital for patient care, society, and general practitioners’ (GPs) wellbeing. Despite its benefits, some GPs attend CME infrequently. While GPs’ preferences for CME are well documented, it is unclear if these preferences are shared by infrequent users. Exploring infrequent CME users’ preferences and educational needs is essential to engage them effectively.
